topic: Why contractors lose jobs to missed calls, and what a voice agent actually does about it

slides.subtitle: (what a missed call actually costs you)
slides.scene: The robot stands beside a large matte navy telephone handset lying on its side on the floor, with a single Scaile blue droplet falling from the earpiece onto the flat white surface below.
The robot stands near the top of a tall white ladder holding a matte navy toolbox with both hands, while a small Scaile blue telephone handset sits ringing on the floor far below.
slides.annotation: the lead was never lost, it was just unanswered
bullets: you are on a roof with both hands full

caption:
Your phone is the leak. Most contractors do not lose jobs on price, they lose them on the call nobody picked up.

1. The call always comes at the worst time. You are on a roof, both hands full, and it rings out.
2. Voicemail is not a safety net. Most callers hang up before the beep, and the ones who do leave a message have booked someone else by the time you ring back.
3. A voice agent books the job. It answers on the first ring, asks what you would ask, and writes it into the calendar.
4. Script it like a dispatcher, not a salesperson. Address and fault first. Hand off to a human the moment money comes up.
5. Test it like it will fail. Call it yourself, mumble, give a bad address, get angry at it. Every agent breaks somewhere and you want to be the one who finds it.

If you want the build plan I use for these, comment DISPATCH and I will send it over.
